one_liner: Intercom has a broad REST API with OAuth 2.0 for public apps, a free developer workspace with access tokens, and an official hosted MCP server.
auth_notes: OAuth 2.0 for public apps accessing other people's data, set up in the Developer Hub. Access tokens are for private apps on your own workspace.
access_notes: Free development workspace (US region only) gives Developer Hub access to configure OAuth and webhooks. It lacks the full functionality of a paid workspace. Review is only needed to publish publicly to the App Store; private apps need no review.
blocker_notes: Free dev workspace gives working credentials. App review applies only to App Store publishing.

evidence.quote: To develop a public app you will need to use a development workspace: [sign up here](https://www.intercom.com/signup/developer) to create your free account.
Development workspaces are only available for the US region.
You can build a private app using your Access Token and it does not require a review.
Connect via the Streamable HTTP endpoint at https://mcp.intercom.com/mcp
Intercom's MCP server lets AI tools and CLIs (like Claude Code, Claude Desktop, ChatGPT, Cursor, and VS Code) securely access your Intercom data through the Model Context Protocol.
If you are building a public integration that will have access to other peoples' Intercom data you are required to set up OAuth.
you can build your own using our [REST APIs](https://developers.intercom.com/docs/build-an-integration/getting-started)
